```spe/prediction-log.md
## Round 2 (closed 2026-10-21)

Source: spe/predictions/r02.yaml (saved before the run) and spe/evals/results/r02/r02.json (5 trials per cell, 40 tickets).
The r02 prediction saved no bands. I scored it with a default band of ±0.05 for accuracy and ±25% for cost. That default is logged in spe/spec/disagreements.md.

| Metric | Config | Predicted | Measured | Same as last round | Verdict | Closer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category_acc (pass rate) | A | 0.85 | 0.86 | 0.84 | hit | prediction |
| category_acc (pass rate) | B | 0.88 | 0.86 | 0.84 | hit | tie (both off by 0.02) |
| category_acc (pass rate) | C | 0.90 | 0.80 | 0.84 | miss | naive guess |
| category_acc (pass rate) | D | 0.75 | 0.74 | 0.70 | hit | prediction |
| priority_acc | C | 0.80 | 0.71 | none recorded | miss | no naive guess to compare |
| cost_per_ticket | D | $0.002 | $0.004 | none recorded | miss | no naive guess to compare |

Score: 3 hits and 3 misses out of 6.

The naive guess beat the predictions on category accuracy. Mean absolute error was 0.030 for the naive guess and 0.035 for the predictions. The miss on C caused the gap. On category accuracy the predictions are not adding value yet.

### Which Why broke

- **C, category_acc and priority_acc.** The Why was "merged tools cut wrong tool choice." The wrong assumption was that a merged tool still makes the agent run every check it needs. C made 2.6 tool calls per ticket. A, B, and D made 3.9 to 4.1. C never called check_status on 9 outage tickets. Category accuracy fell to 0.80 and priority accuracy fell to 0.71. See F4.
- **D, cost_per_ticket.** The Why was "same design on a smaller model loses about 0.15." That line was about accuracy, and it held: D lost 0.12 against A, which is inside the band. The cost number had no Why of its own. It assumed one model pass per ticket. D retried on tickets over 2,000 words, and each retry doubled the tokens. See F5.
- **B, category_acc (hit, but the Why is unsupported).** The Why was "shorter prompt keeps focus." B tied A at 0.86, so the run shows no accuracy gain from the shorter prompt. B did cost less, at $0.009 against $0.011.
```

```spe/failures.md
### F4. Merged tool skips the status check

- **Kind:** agent (configuration design). **Round:** r02.
- **What:** Config C merges the tools into fewer calls. C never called check_status on 9 outage tickets. C averaged 2.6 tool calls per ticket. The other configs averaged 3.9 to 4.1. C scored 0.80 on category accuracy and 0.71 on priority accuracy. A scored 0.86 and 0.79.
- **How to spot it:** For every ticket labeled outage, check the tool-call log for a check_status call. Treat a config whose mean tool calls fall well below the others as a warning.
- **Seen in:** trials r02-C-T17-1 to r02-C-T17-3, on 9 outage tickets, as listed in the r02.json notes.
- **Fix:** open. Proposals r03-1 and r03-4 in spe/spec/spec.md.

### F5. Smaller model retries long tickets and doubles tokens

- **Kind:** agent. **Round:** r02.
- **What:** Config D retried on tickets over 2,000 words. Each retry doubled the tokens for that ticket. D cost $0.004 per ticket. The prediction was $0.002.
- **How to spot it:** Count the model calls per ticket and flag any ticket with more than one. Compare tokens per ticket against ticket word count.
- **Seen in:** r02 D cells, on tickets over 2,000 words. The r02.json notes do not list trial ids. Pull them from the D transcripts before r03 specify.
- **Fix:** open. Proposal r03-2 in spe/spec/spec.md.

No regrade happened in r02. No grader bug was found after the run.
```
